A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with matching authors, title, methods, and experiments. All 19 pages of each version, including figures, equations, tables, and Appendices A–B, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original NIH evaluations, attention-steering interventions, instruction-finetuning experiments, and appendix analyses of thresholds, layers, and training-data characteristics.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical experiments and appendix analyses, with revised results in the main QA comparisons.

M1.justification: Attention steering, the context-dependency score, retrieval-head selection, and conditional finetuning with [IND] remain unchanged. The expanded explanation of model-dependent context reliance does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both use ShareGPT, UltraChat-200K, and WizardLM-70K for finetuning and evaluate NIH, SQuAD, QuAC, DROP, and MT-Bench. No dataset, task, or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain vanilla finetuning, official Llama-2/Llama-3 instruct models, and the same attention-steering and chat-template controls. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.3 changes the reported NIH metric from recall error to recall, and v3 Table 3 removes the aggregate Avg. metric from v2 Table 4. These are reporting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that the experiments were rerun or that QA scoring procedures changed.

E4.justification: The attention-steering intervention evidence is revised: Table 1 changes the Llama-2-7B QuAC comparison from a small improvement, 0.1330 to 0.1340, to a tie, 22.20 to 22.20. The appendix threshold ablation, layer-agreement analysis, and instruction-length analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across four NIH prompt templates for smaller settings, with single-template reporting for larger settings. The new main-text mention of rerunning different prompts repeats information already present in v2 Appendix A.2.

E6.justification: A substantial portion of the central QA evidence changes in v2 Table 4 versus v3 Table 3. Expressing both in percentages, ShareGPT/TinyLlama SQuAD changes from 59.18/61.44 to 59.73/62.05 for vanilla/indicator; ShareGPT/Llama-3 QuAC changes from 15.60/16.60 to 24.80/24.50, reversing their ranking. Table 1 QuAC scores also change, and aggregate averages disappear. NIH, DROP, MT-Bench, and appendix results remain numerically unchanged after accounting for unit conversions.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects a mathematical definition: v2 labels the retrieved-keyword fraction as error, whereas v3 calls it recall and defines error as 1 minus recall. The method equations and appendix head-selection definition remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the claim of being first and replaces partial causation and hypothesis validation with association and correlation. The introduction explicitly qualifies the observation to open-source models. The central indicator-based contribution and claims about preserving context awareness and general capabilities remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains why context dependency also depends on a model's existing knowledge and acknowledges that attention bias provides an incomplete explanation. Section 4.2 emphasizes dataset sparsity when interpreting DROP and MT-Bench behavior. Conversely, the limitations remove v2's discussion of users needing to determine when the indicator is appropriate.

D1.justification: Section 2.1 newly documents removing newlines around the NIH needle and scoring the first 100 generated tokens. Appendix A.3 still specifies a 50-token generation cap, leaving the relationship unclear. The main-text QLoRA-on-transformer-layers statement disappears, although Appendix A.1.1 retains the QLoRA recipes; an actual training-method change is not established.

R1.justification: The bibliography removes Kamradt (2023) and Dettmers et al. (2024), and the abstract withdraws its priority claim. The comparison with An et al. moves from Section 3.2 to Section 5; it is not newly introduced positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, method motivation, results discussion, and limitations. Contribution bullets are consolidated, and a short Impact Statement is added. The overall section sequence and most technical and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 are reduced and moved onto page 3, and attention-chart axes and labels switch to percentage units. The main Tables 3–4 exchange order, the performance table loses its Avg. column, and Table 9 moves beside its discussion. Several tables become more compact; no figure or table is newly added.

improvement.justification: Correcting the recall-error definition and tempering causal and priority claims improve clarity. However, revised main QA scores are not reconciled with the unchanged values in Appendix Table 9, and Section 4.2 claims consistent gains despite the QuAC reversal in Table 3. Removing the indicator-selection limitation also weakens qualification. These benefits and reporting problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
